title: Investigate an outage
question: Why is checkout timing out?
description: A deployment looks guilty. Duplicate alerts repeat the same signal. Independent traces then point to connection exhaustion.
when: Use when an incident agent must preserve competing causes, separate repeated alerts from independent corroboration, and revise an investigation as telemetry arrives.
alternative: A simple search retrieves relevant logs; the investigator still has to track independence, contradictions and decision changes.
hypotheses: The new release caused checkout failures
Database connection exhaustion caused checkout failures

events.content: 09:02 — Checkout timeouts start four minutes after release 4.8.
09:03 — Pager notification copies the same deployment-monitor alert.
09:05 — Replay of the release change reproduces elevated checkout errors.
09:08 — A separate connection-pool trace shows all 80 connections occupied.
09:10 — Timeouts persist after a complete release rollback.
09:11 — Database metrics independently show connection wait queues at saturation.
09:13 — Releasing leaked connections restores checkout in a controlled replay.
09:15 — The release replay used the wrong configuration; withdraw it.

title: Keep agent memory current
question: Which fulfilment region should the assistant use?
description: A stale EU preference keeps resurfacing. An authenticated update and independent order records support US fulfilment.
when: Use when a long-running assistant must retire outdated facts without losing provenance, and recover stored evidence after reopening its database.
alternative: Last-write-wins can be enough for a single authoritative preference. MoolBase adds value when several sources disagree and provenance matters.
hypotheses: Use EU fulfilment for this account
Use US fulfilment for this account

events.content: March 1 — Authenticated account profile requests EU fulfilment.
March 2 — Separate account-manager call confirms the EU preference.
March 3 — A copied CRM summary repeats the old account profile.
April 1 — Authenticated user changes fulfilment to the US.
April 2 — A separate recorded user call confirms the US move.
April 3 — A verified order is successfully shipped from the US warehouse.
April 4 — The account manager retires the March call as outdated.
April 4 — The derived CRM cache is also retired explicitly.

title: Challenge conflicting reports
question: What is the delivery window for part K-42?
description: A widely repeated seven-day claim competes with supplier data. Unverified claims remain distinct from certified observations.
when: Use when a research or procurement agent must retain conflicting claims, show unresolved uncertainty, and reconsider its answer after source corrections.
alternative: A source list shows where claims came from. It does not automatically group copied sources or emit a governed revision receipt.

events.content: May 1 — A verified supplier catalogue lists a seven-day lead time.
May 2 — A distributor republishes the same catalogue statement.
May 3 — An independent verified sales call quotes seven days.
May 4 — An unverified forum post claims a 21-day backlog.
May 5 — Supplier issues a signed correction: the catalogue is outdated.
May 6 — A verified production schedule shows a 21-day backlog.
May 7 — An independent warehouse audit confirms no immediate stock.
May 8 — A signed order acknowledgement confirms delivery in 21 days.
May 9 — Supplier withdraws the old catalogue entry.
